texto: Would I rather be feared or loved? Easy. Both. I want people to be afraid of how much they love me.
nota: Machiavelli wrote that it's safer to be feared. Michael only read half and wanted both.

texto: Sometimes I'll start a sentence and I don't even know where it's going. I just hope I find it along the way.
nota: Michael calls this an "improversation". Philosophers call it not having a plan.

texto: I'm not superstitious, but I am a little stitious.
nota: No philosopher ever invented a word this fast. Or this badly.

texto: Wikipedia is the best thing ever. Anyone in the world can write anything they want about any subject, so you know you are getting the best possible information.
nota: Irony: the photo on this badge came from Wikipedia. Michael would be proud.

texto: Society teaches us that having feelings and crying is bad and wrong. Well, that's baloney, because grief isn't wrong.
nota: He said this at the funeral he organized for a bird. Speech included.

texto: And I knew exactly what to do. But in a much more real sense, I had no idea what to do.
nota: Socrates admitted he didn't know. Michael manages to know and not know at the same time.

texto: Do I need to be liked? Absolutely not. I like to be liked. I enjoy being liked. I have to be liked. But it's not like this compulsive need to be liked. Like my need to be praised.
nota: Says he doesn't need it. Repeats it four times. Needs it.

texto: Make friends first, make sales second, make love third. In no particular order.
nota: A sales strategy no management handbook would ever approve. In no particular order.

texto: I'm an early bird and I'm a night owl. So I'm wise and I have worms.
nota: Two proverbs walked into a sentence. Only a Michael came out.

texto: Fool me once, strike one. But fool me twice… strike three.
nota: He mixed a proverb with baseball. Both lost.

texto: Webster's Dictionary defines wedding as the fusing of two metals with a hot torch.
nota: He said this at a wedding, into a microphone. Nobody stopped him.

texto: Whenever I'm about to do something, I think, 'Would an idiot do that?' And if they would, I do not do that thing.
nota: A flawless philosophical test. Dwight just never applied it to Dwight.

texto: Through concentration, I can raise and lower my cholesterol at will.
nota: Medically impossible. Spiritually, very Dwight.

texto: I never smile if I can help it. Showing one's teeth is a submission signal in primates.
nota: Dwight read one book about primates and took it way too seriously. Like everything.

texto: People underestimate the power of nostalgia. Nostalgia is truly one of the great human weaknesses, second only to the neck.
nota: Starts like a poet, ends like a martial arts manual.

texto: In the wild, there is no health care. Ow, I hurt my leg, I can't run, a lion eats me and I'm dead. Well, I'm not dead. I'm the lion.
nota: Started talking about health insurance and ended up at the top of the food chain.

texto: I am fast. To give you a reference point, I am somewhere between a snake and a mongoose… and a panther.
nota: A résumé written by a wildlife documentary.

texto: Not everything is a lesson. Sometimes you just fail.
nota: Sounds like Marcus Aurelius. It was said to a temp after his first failed sale.

texto: How would I describe myself? Three words. Hardworking. Alpha male. Jackhammer. Merciless. Insatiable.
nota: Three words. Five words. Zero shame.

texto: I don't have a lot of experience with vampires, but I have hunted werewolves. I shot one once, but by the time I got to it, it had turned back into my neighbor's dog.
nota: Vampires? Not convinced. Werewolves are another story.

texto: Nothing stresses me out. Except having to seek the approval of my inferiors.
nota: Stress management, beet farm style.

texto: What does not kill me makes me stronger.
nota: Nietzsche said it first. Dwight just owns the beet farm.
fonte: Twilight of the Idols, Maxims and Arrows, 8

texto: Without music, life would be a mistake.
nota: A quote worthy of a motivational poster in Michael's office.
fonte: Twilight of the Idols, Maxims and Arrows, 33

texto: In individuals, insanity is rare; but in groups, parties, nations and epochs, it is the rule.
nota: Nietzsche never worked at Dunder Mifflin, but he described it perfectly.

texto: The unexamined life is not worth living.
nota: Michael examines his life every single day. Out loud. To the camera.

texto: I am a sort of gadfly, given to the city by the god; the city is like a great and noble horse, slow because of its size, that needs to be stirred into life.
nota: Socrates stinging Athens is Dwight stinging Jim. Just with a toga.

texto: Wonder is the feeling of a philosopher, and philosophy begins in wonder.
nota: Wonder is the feeling of a philosopher. And of Pam, every time Michael opens his mouth.

texto: Is it not delightful to have friends coming from distant quarters?
nota: That's Michael whenever someone from corporate visits Scranton.

texto: I have not seen one who loves virtue as he loves beauty.
nota: Written 2,500 years ago. Still describes half the office.

texto: To see what is right and not to do it is want of courage.
nota: Dwight would quote this right before snitching to Michael.

texto: Begin the morning by saying to yourself: I shall meet with the busybody, the ungrateful, arrogant, deceitful, envious, unsocial.
nota: A Roman emperor describing a Monday at Dunder Mifflin.

texto: The art of life is more like the wrestler's art than the dancer's.
nota: Dwight agrees. That's why he chose karate over ballet.

texto: The best way of avenging yourself is not to become like the wrongdoer.
nota: Advice Dwight never followed. Neither did Jim.

texto: All warfare is based on deception.
nota: Jim's motto every time he pranks Dwight.

texto: Let your plans be dark and impenetrable as night, and when you move, fall like a thunderbolt.
nota: This is underlined in Dwight's copy. Twice.

texto: The supreme art of war is to subdue the enemy without fighting.
nota: Michael's strategy for firing someone: never doing it.
